title: Philippines BPO Client SLA Monitor
thesis: Snowflake turns daily activity from 40 synthetic client programs of a fictional Philippine BPO into SLA and incident KPIs, 7-day SLA-breach risk scores, abandon-rate anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: Incident-free contact rate, incidents raised, SLA-breach incidents and billable value for 40 client programs served from Taguig City, Pasig City, Cebu City, Davao City and Bacolod City.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to program-day rows.
The incident-type chart shows which disruptions cost the daily service level and which always resolve, such as area power interruptions.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of client SLA KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which programs should workforce planning watch first?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each program's probability of an SLA-breach incident in the next 7 days.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent 14 labelled days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags abandon-rate outliers per program, and the forecast projects incident volume across all programs for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

talking_points: QA calibration compliance, client document coverage and pending documents frame the quality and contract gaps.
Calibration compliance against SLA breaches by program shows where missed audits and breaches move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised actions from the KPI, program, incident-type and risk tables only.
show: QA calibration compliance and document coverage
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when a queue hits trouble right now?

talking_points: Live contact events land in RAW.LIVE_CONTACTS, from the simulator or from Amazon Data Firehose through Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs INCIDENT events with an SOP hint and the program's current risk band, then emails the on-call analyst.
tabs.call_out: From queue incident to ticket in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over 14 synthetic incident-handling SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (Data Firehose, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
